clue.text: Pause at these, I fancy

indicators.note: to fancy something up is to dress it in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a reader would stop and think at these lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as a polite aside, but fancy is the signal and I is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to stop briefly in doubt, a direct synonym of pause as a verb.

clue.text: Soldier, American, stopping reckless climbing

indicators.note: stopping a gap means plugging it, so one piece sits inside the other
in a down clue, climbing means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rash means acting without care
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A US soldier is caught scrambling up something carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the reversal reads upward, so the climbing word is reversed before the American piece goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry trooper, a specific kind of soldier.

clue.text: Throwing darts, gets honour and fame

indicators.note: throwing scatters things, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A darts player wins an award and becomes a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit (OM) is an honour given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the state of being a celebrity, a close synonym of fame.

clue.text: Possessed by lanneret, a long claw

indicators.note: what is possessed by these words is held within them, sitting inside the run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of lanneret, a and the start of long

explanation.surface: A lanneret, a small falcon, owns a long claw.
explanation.walkthrough: A lanneret is a male falcon, so the claw fits the picture neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Believe magazine is to go on a campaign

parts.note: to take something as true is to believe it, as in 'I take it'
The Field is a long-running British country-sports magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine sets out to launch a campaign it believes in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Field is a British magazine on hunting, shooting and the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An army takes the field when it begins a military campaign; the idiom also covers starting any contest.

clue.text: Instruments for travelling salesmen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: means by which something is done
second meaning: representatives who sell on behalf of a firm

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tools sold door to door; the two parts are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the means or cause of an effect and people acting as representatives for a business.

clue.text: Rodent from African country, and farm animal

parts.note: Guinea is a West African nation
a pig is kept on a farm

explanation.surface: A rodent comes from Africa, along with a farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The guinea pig, or cavy, is a small South American rodent kept as a pet.

clue.text: African country ban I aim to change

indicators.note: changing the words means altering their order into something new

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A politician declares an intention to lift a ban in an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a nation in south-west Africa, bordering South Africa and Angola.

clue.text: Eagles shot across northern African country

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it, so one piece wraps around the other
something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Eagles are shot flying over northern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: EAGLES reworked as SE...EGAL takes N into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a West African nation on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Ankle was twisted in ballet

indicators.note: a twisted thing is bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A dancer sprains an ankle during a ballet performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's famous ballet, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Flyer needed by funfair manager

indicators.note: what one word needs from another is held inside it, here straddling two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of funfair and the start of manager

explanation.surface: A funfair manager needs a leaflet printed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a handbill advertising the fair; here it is a person who flies.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman is a pilot or member of an air force, someone who flies.

clue.text: One teaching in the classroom, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of many arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone who teaches stands in the classroom, presumably.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, with the twelve letters of 'the classroom' giving the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a male teacher at a school, one whose job is teaching.

clue.text: Poet in university in former British colony

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: Aden, now in Yemen, was a British colony until 1967
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A poet is at a university in an old British colony.
explanation.walkthrough: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet; Aden was a British colony in southern Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was a major twentieth-century writer of verse.

clue.text: Put food in this stuff on barge at sea

parts.note: to tuck in is to stuff oneself with food, and tuck is also British slang for food

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone is told to load food aboard a barge going out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put food in this' reads as an instruction, but it is the definition. A tucker-bag is an Australian bushman's food bag; tucker is Australian slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tucker-bag is the bag an Australian traveller carries provisions in, so food is put in it.

clue.text: Girl's old lady finds something in an oyster, perhaps

parts.note: 'old lady' is informal slang for one's mother
the possessive ending read as 'belonging to'
Pearl is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's mother opens an oyster and finds something inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's old lady' is turned round: the old lady of Pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl is the iridescent nacre lining the shells of oysters and other molluscs.

clue.text: Little time to study philosopher's routine

parts.note: T is the short form of time
to read a subject at university is to study it
John Stuart Mill was a nineteenth-century English philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher's daily habit leaves only a little time for study.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively a tedious, unvarying routine of work.

clue.text: Comedian in lace factory heading off for Wigan

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its front letter

parts.note: to lace a drink is to spike it with alcohol
a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill
the Lancashire town, taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian working in a lace factory sets off for Wigan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lace factory' suggests textiles, but lace is a verb here. Spike Milligan was a comedian of The Goon Show; Wigan is a town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike Milligan was a celebrated British comic writer and performer, best known for The Goon Show.

clue.text: What may be sown in Isle of Wight resort?

wordplay.note: the word sown is spelt S followed by own

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what crops might be planted around an island holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What may be sown' suggests seeds, but it asks how the word sown can be described: S and OWN. Sandown is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandown is a seaside holiday town on the east coast of the Isle of Wight.

clue.text: One about to be strangled by evil Italian criminal

parts.note: ill can mean evil, as in ill will

indicators.note: something strangled is gripped all round the middle, so it ends up enclosed

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian
c is short for circa, about
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Italian gangster plans to strangle someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun for the gangster, but it is an adjective here; c is the abbreviation of circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law, so criminal is an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Bouquet may make beak happy

parts.note: beak is slang for a person's nose
gay in its older sense of light-hearted and cheerful

explanation.surface: Flowers might please a bird's beak.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouquet also suggests a wine's aroma, which would fit the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of fragrant flowers, a little bouquet.

clue.text: Clubs, later, reformed syndicate

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: something reformed is formed again in a new shape, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Some clubs later band together in a new syndicate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is an association of businesses that fix prices together, a type of syndicate.

clue.text: Entailed trips crossing lake in part of Egypt

indicators.note: crossing means going over and round something, so one piece is wrapped inside the other
something that trips stumbles and tumbles, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A tour involved boat trips over a lake in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entailed trips' looks like a description of a journey, but trips signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile Delta is the fan-shaped region of northern Egypt where the Nile meets the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Arabs murdered in Iraqi port

indicators.note: something murdered is destroyed, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A news report of Arabs killed in an Iraqi port.
explanation.definitionFit: Basra is Iraq's main seaport, on the Shatt al-Arab waterway.

clue.text: Former PM in black hole

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a lair is an animal's den, a hole it hides in

explanation.surface: A former prime minister finds himself in a dark hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was the British Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007.

clue.text: Gold cross initially concealed in plant

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of cross
hid means kept out of sight

explanation.surface: A gold cross is hidden away among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concealed in' suggests a hidden word, but concealed is a plain synonym and in is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant of a large family prized for showy blooms.

clue.text: Neat poker hand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: undiluted, as a drink served without water
second meaning: five cards in sequence

explanation.walkthrough: Neat seems to describe the poker hand as tidy; it is a separate meaning, of spirits served undiluted.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit drunk neat is taken undiluted, and in poker the word names five cards of consecutive rank.

clue.text: Annoy the Parisian after final

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the answer

parts.note: nett, the older spelling of net, describes the final figure after all deductions
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Parisian is irritated after losing a final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' looks like a noun, a match, but it is the adjective, as in a final total.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate them, as a stinging plant would.

clue.text: Two kings on board a majestic flagship of yore

parts.note: taken as written
R for rex and K for king, two abbreviations for a king
royal means befitting a monarch

explanation.surface: Two kings are aboard a majestic old flagship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a container, but the pieces simply run in order. Ark Royal is the name of several Royal Navy ships, including aircraft-carrier flagships.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Ark Royal has been the name of several Royal Navy flagships, back to the Armada.
